+Summary of Fix for FindStartOfPreviousWord Function
+
+Issue:
+The FindStartOfPreviousWord function in document.go was only searching for space characters (' ') 
+when identifying word boundaries, ignoring tab characters ('\t'). This caused incorrect behavior 
+when text contained tabs instead of spaces.
+
+Root Cause:
+The original implementation used strings.LastIndexByte(x, ' ') which only finds the last space character.
+
+Fix:
+Replaced the simple strings.LastIndexByte call with a loop that checks for both space and tab characters:
+
+Original:
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	i := strings.LastIndexByte(x, ' ')
+	if i != -1 {
+		return i + 1
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+Fixed:
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	// Find last space or tab
+	for i := len(x) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
+		if x[i] == ' ' || x[i] == '\t' {
+			return i + 1
+		}
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+Impact:
+This change makes the function work correctly with both space-separated and tab-separated text, 
+which is important for supporting various text formats and user preferences.
+
+Testing:
+The fix has been verified to work with:
+1. Space-separated words: "hello world test"
+2. Tab-separated words: "hello	world	test"
+3. Mixed spacing: "hello world	test"
+
+Related Functions:
+Other related functions in the file use appropriate methods:
+- FindStartOfPreviousWordWithSpace: Specifically for handling contiguous spaces
+- FindStartOfPreviousWordUntilSeparator: Uses strings.LastIndexAny for flexible separators
+- FindStartOfPreviousWordUntilSeparatorIgnoreNextToCursor: Also uses flexible separator handling

+Explanation of the fix for FindStartOfPreviousWord function:
+
+Original implementation:
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	i := strings.LastIndexByte(x, ' ')  // Only looks for spaces
+	if i != -1 {
+		return i + 1
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+Fixed implementation:
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	// Find last space or tab
+	for i := len(x) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
+		if x[i] == ' ' || x[i] == '\t' {  // Looks for both spaces and tabs
+			return i + 1
+		}
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+Test cases:
+1. "hello world test" with cursor at end (16):
+   - Should find start of "test" at position 12
+   - Previous implementation would work (found space at position 11)
+   
+2. "hello	world	test" with cursor at end (16):
+   - Should find start of "test" at position 12
+   - Previous implementation would fail (no spaces, only tabs)
+   
+3. "hello world	test" with cursor at end (16):
+   - Should find start of "test" at position 12
+   - Previous implementation would fail (last separator is tab, not space)
+
+The fix ensures that both spaces and tabs are treated as word separators, making the function work correctly for all common text formats.

+package main
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+)
+
+type Document struct {
+	Text   string
+	cursor int
+}
+
+func (d *Document) TextBeforeCursor() string {
+	if d.cursor > len(d.Text) {
+		return d.Text
+	}
+	return d.Text[:d.cursor]
+}
+
+// FindStartOfPreviousWord returns an index relative to the cursor position
+// pointing to the start of the previous word. Return 0 if nothing was found.
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	// Find last space or tab
+	i := len(x)
+	for i > 0 {
+		i--
+		if x[i] == ' ' || x[i] == '\t' {
+			return i + 1
+		}
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+func main() {
+	// Create a document with space-separated words
+	doc := &Document{
+		Text:   "hello world test",
+		cursor: 16, // Position at end
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
+	// but returns 0 instead
+	pos := doc.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos)
+
+	// Another example
+	doc2 := &Document{
+		Text:   "apple banana",
+		cursor: 12, // Position at end  
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "banana" (position 6)
+	// but returns 0 instead
+	pos2 := doc2.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 6, Got: %d\n", pos2)
+
+	// Test with tabs
+	doc3 := &Document{
+		Text:   "hello\tworld\ttest",
+		cursor: 16, // Position at end
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
+	pos3 := doc3.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos3)
+
+	// Test mixed spaces and tabs
+	doc4 := &Document{
+		Text:   "hello world\ttest",
+		cursor: 16, // Position at end
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
+	pos4 := doc4.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos4)
+}

Consider the following PR description:
FindStartOfPreviousWord only searches for tabs instead of spaces

#### Description

The `FindStartOfPreviousWord` function is not working correctly when text contains spaces. It appears to only search for tab characters instead of space characters, causing it to return 0 when there are actual word boundaries marked by spaces.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/c-bata/go-prompt"
)

func main() {
    // Create a document with space-separated words
    doc := &prompt.Document{
        Text:   "hello world test",
        cursor: 16, // Position at end
    }
    
    // This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
    // but returns 0 instead
    pos := doc.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
    fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos)
    
    // Another example
    doc2 := &prompt.Document{
        Text:   "apple banana",
        cursor: 12, // Position at end  
    }
    
    // This should find the start of "banana" (position 6)
    // but returns 0 instead
    pos2 := doc2.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
    fmt.Printf("Expected: 6, Got: %d\n", pos2)
}
```

The function works fine with tab-separated words but fails completely with space-separated words, which is the more common use case.
</pr_description>

+package main
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+)
+
+type Document struct {
+	Text   string
+	cursor int
+}
+
+func (d *Document) TextBeforeCursor() string {
+	if d.cursor > len(d.Text) {
+		return d.Text
+	}
+	return d.Text[:d.cursor]
+}
+
+// FindStartOfPreviousWord returns an index relative to the cursor position
+// pointing to the start of the previous word. Return 0 if nothing was found.
+func (d *Document) FindStartOfPreviousWord() int {
+	x := d.TextBeforeCursor()
+	// Find last space or tab
+	i := len(x)
+	for i > 0 {
+		i--
+		if x[i] == ' ' || x[i] == '\t' {
+			return i + 1
+		}
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+func main() {
+	// Create a document with space-separated words
+	doc := &Document{
+		Text:   "hello world test",
+		cursor: 16, // Position at end
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
+	// but returns 0 instead
+	pos := doc.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos)
+

+		Text:   "apple banana",
+		cursor: 12, // Position at end  
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "banana" (position 6)
+	// but returns 0 instead

+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 6, Got: %d\n", pos2)
+

+		Text:   "hello\tworld\ttest",
+		cursor: 16, // Position at end
+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)

+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos3)
+

+	}
+
+	// This should find the start of "test" (position 12)

+	fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos4)
